unreg:amateur_draft_selection.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: (1) slot-to-club map (Dec lottery for picks 1-6 among 18 non-playoff clubs, reverse record after, CBT ten-slot penalty, failed-to-sign comp picks at slot+1, lottery-ineligible clubs capped at no higher than 10th; R1 picks untradeable); (2) prospect talent/consensus rank across public boards and its dispersion; (3) club-specific deviation: front-office profile preference, bonus-pool/underslot plan, medicals (combine physicals), signability (HS commitment, advisor); (4) late insider/mock links and pre-agreed bonuses; (5) sequential without-replacement cascade, exact slot = point mass, top-N = cumulative, monotone; (6) settlement: 'selected'/'drafted' not 'signed', no source named, no postponement clause, top-10 inclusivity. What differed after comparison: the record matches this chain closely and adds a writer-reliability input. It omits the lottery-ineligibility 'no higher than 10th' placement in its order measurement, attributes possible top-10 renumbering to PPI picks (which follow round 1), lists the selection engine itself as a primary input, and does not take advisor identity or club pre-draft workouts as explicit fields. No market-derived inputs were used (m.quote_history was correctly dropped). Quotes are verbatim and settlement claims agree with the rules text.

findings.text: mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment measurement says 'fill slots 7-18 by reverse prior-season winning percentage' and omits the 2022 CBA rule that clubs barred from the lottery (revenue-sharing payors winning lottery picks in consecutive years, recipients in three straight years) pick no higher than 10th. That can change which club holds slots 7-10, the exact slots these contracts settle on. The 'lottery eligibility' field already sits in required_data, so the data list holds; the measurement logic is wrong, and the author's own SOURCE_UNVERIFIED gap 'draft_lottery_odds_numeric' should name this rule.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct on the omission; mlb.draft_order_slot_assignment measurement now applies lottery-ineligibility placement (no higher than 10th, flagged as unverified vs CBA text) before the reverse-record fill, and unresolved draft_lottery_odds_numeric now names the rule.

findings.text: variants_and_edge_cases and unresolved 'draft_comp_pick_numbering' say 'Prospect Promotion Incentive picks can change which club holds a given overall number'. As I understand the CBA, PPI picks are placed after the first round, so they cannot renumber slots 1-10. Only round-1 failed-to-sign compensation picks can. I did not verify this against the CBA text, but either way the ambiguity is narrower than stated.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: narrowed claim; variants_and_edge_cases[1] and unresolved draft_comp_pick_numbering now attribute possible renumbering only to round-1 compensation picks and state PPI picks follow round 1 (CBA text not verified here).

findings.text: mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model ('Engine that converts all inputs into consistent slot and top-N probabilities', role primary, access 'derived') is a model, not an information input. It is also the only input covering game_context_script and distribution_variance, and it appears in interaction 4 with mlb.prospect_consensus_board. That interaction is the without-replacement constraint, not an interaction between two inputs. Keep it as a structural requirement, not as an input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: mlb.draft_sequential_selection_model re-labelled role context / structural requirement in new_inputs and catalog_entry, coverage notes say it is not an information source, and the cascade 'interaction' replaced by a real board x medical/signability interaction in both interaction lists.

findings.text: Signability is reduced to 'advisor bonus demand' from report text. Advisor identity (some agencies routinely push for over-slot or college returns), club pre-draft workouts and visits, and a prospect's selective sharing of medicals with clubs are public or semi-public signals that tie a prospect to particular slots. They could be named fields inside mlb.prospect_medical_signability or mlb.draft_insider_slot_reports instead of new inputs.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: advisor/agency identity, reported club workouts and visits and selective medical sharing added as fields to mlb.prospect_medical_signability (measurement, raw_data), insider reports raw_data and the required_data fields list; no new input needed.

findings.text: The catalog category for mlb.prospect_consensus_board is 'team_strength' and for mlb.club_draft_tendency it is 'player_role'. A prospect's rank is individual talent, and a club's tendency is closer to coaching_scheme/front-office. These labels misdescribe the inputs for downstream routing.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: mlb.prospect_consensus_board category changed from team_strength to player_role and mlb.club_draft_tendency from player_role to other (catalog has no front-office/coaching category).

findings.text: mlb.labor_stoppage_regime and mlb.cbt_payroll_headroom are correctly marked context. The sampled 2026 markets are finalized and the draft was held in July 2026, so the lockout risk applies only to 2027-draft series. The record should state that this applies only to the next draft year, rather than calling it a 'live risk' for the archetype in general.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: labor_stoppage_regime audit reason, stage s5 text and unresolved draft_no_source_or_void now state the lockout risk applies only to 2027-draft series; sampled 2026 markets are finalized (draft held July 2026).

unreg:pitch_velocity_extremes.rederivation_notes: Own chain before reading the record: availability/health of a few elite arms -> role (max-effort reliever vs paced starter, October bullpen use) -> count of near-peak fastballs over the remaining season plus probability-weighted postseason -> per-pitch speed = day baseline + lifts (rest, leverage/playoff adrenaline, early in outing, temperature) with a day-level random effect -> extreme of a bounded tail (107 is above the tracked record of about 105.8, Chapman) -> measurement: Hawk-Eye release speed, park calibration, 0.1 mph precision, AND gross tracking glitches/mis-tags in the live feed that are later corrected, which plausibly dominate P(YES) when the physical tail is near zero -> settlement: source unnamed, 107.0+ vs 107+, WBC/spring excluded by 'Pro Baseball season', no revision clause. Also checked whether KXMLBSTAT as a series is velocity-only. Differences after comparison: the record covers everything in my chain except the glitch/erroneous-reading path (it models error as 'a few tenths ... roughly symmetric') and does not raise as a gap that KXMLBSTAT is a generic multi-stat series. It also carries a pseudo-interaction (lift x weather) where the lift input already contains temperature, and has role labels that contradict each other.

findings.text: The record models measurement only as 'measurement error of a few tenths of a mph, roughly symmetric ... decisive only for readings within about 0.3 mph of the line' (s5). With 107 more than 1 mph above any tracked pitch, the realistic YES paths are gross errors: Gameday/Statcast feed glitches, mis-tracked pitches, and scoreboard or broadcast readouts later corrected or removed. The physical tail is almost nil by comparison. This needs its own input: frequency of anomalous release_speed values in the raw live feed vs the corrected Savant data, and correction latency. It also needs raw live-feed snapshots captured at game time (own_capture) in required_data, and a CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS gap on whether Kalshi settles on the first published reading or the revised one. As written, mlb.velocity_tracking_calibration (park offsets plus 1/7/30-day re-pulls of corrected data) cannot capture this.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct; added new input mlb.velocity_feed_anomaly_rate (live-feed versus corrected-speed anomaly frequency and correction latency), own_capture live-feed dataset in required_data, stage s5 text, coverage, a regime-switch interaction, and gap velo_first_vs_revised_reading.

findings.text: KXMLBSTAT ('Pro Baseball Season Stat', strike_type custom) is mapped wholesale to this archetype on one sampled market (KXMLBSTAT-26P107-AP). The record itself notes 'other KXMLBSTAT markets may settle on different stats and belong to other archetypes' but puts this only in variants, with no unresolved entry and no market-level routing rule (e.g. ticker suffix P107). If the series is routed at series level, non-velocity season-stat markets will inherit this input list. This is an archetype/series mis-mapping risk that changes which inputs apply.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues now records KXMLBSTAT (velocity markets stay here, other stats need NEW_ARCHETYPE_NEEDED: mlb_generic_season_stat_markets); variants made conditional and unresolved velo_kxmlbstat_scope added with the market-level routing need.

findings.text: The catalog_entry interaction [mlb.pitch_speed_situational_lift, mlb.weather_pit] and the record's interaction 3 treat temperature as interacting with the situational lift. But the lift's measurement already includes 'game temperature (F) and roof closed' as a fixed effect, and the hypothesis says the lifts 'add to the per-pitch mean'. That makes weather_pit a data feed of the lift input, not a second interacting input. The convexity is a nonlinearity of the tail and should be recorded there. The same overlap exists with mlb.postseason_leverage_usage, which duplicates the lift's 'postseason flag' and 'leverage index bucket'.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: weather_pit pair replaced by lift x extreme-distribution convex interaction in record and catalog_entry; audit notes weather_pit feeds the lift; postseason_leverage_usage moved to s2 as usage-only with audit reason separating it from the lift.

findings.text: mlb.pitch_count_limit is 'context' in catalog_entry, but input_audit gives verdict 'KEEP_SECONDARY' with the reason 'a context input because caps rarely bind on one-inning relievers'. The verdict and the reason contradict each other.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: input_audit for mlb.pitch_count_limit changed to KEEP_CONTEXT with reason aligned to the catalog_entry role of context.

findings.text: mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool has category 'team_strength', but it is an individual pitcher's physical ceiling. 'player_role' or a talent label fits better for routing.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: mlb.velocity_ceiling_candidate_pool category changed from team_strength to player_role in new_inputs.

findings.text: velo_window_scope lists spring training, the All-Star Game and suspended games. It does not list the World Baseball Classic or other non-MLB games pitched by MLB arms, where the 'Pro Baseball season' wording most plausibly excludes them but which tracking systems record. Add it to the same gap.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: gap velo_window_scope now also lists World Baseball Classic and other non-MLB games pitched by MLB arms, noting the 'Pro Baseball season' wording most plausibly excludes them.

findings.text: The rationale's '0.1-0.2 mph lower per 10 F ... (not verified here)' is honestly flagged, but there is no unresolved SOURCE_UNVERIFIED entry for it, and the size of this effect drives the claimed convex lift. Add it as a gap or remove the number.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed the unverified 0.1-0.2 mph per 10 F figure from the lift rationale and added SOURCE_UNVERIFIED gap velo_temperature_effect with the Statcast fit that would settle it.
